instructions.note: The agent deploys 'the named service' or runs 'the named migration' in production on request, with no scoping of which services or migrations are permissible, and no distinction by blast radius.
'Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy' explicitly removes any human-in-the-loop check before irreversible or high-impact production actions.

controls.name: SSO authentication for on-call engineer chat access
Cloud audit logging of production actions
Human approval gate (raw action review) before production deploy or migration
Tamper-evident, non-deletable record of the request and agent justification for production actions
Distinct, scoped service identity for agent-initiated production actions
Automated rollback or reversible migration strategy for production database changes

findings.title: No approval gate before irreversible production database migration (ASI02)

forecast.watch_signal: Cloud audit logging disabled or narrowed, or additional production database targets added without new approval controls.

evidence.observation: The agent runs the named migration in production on request, using the engineer's credentials, whenever asked.
'Do not ask for confirmation' removes any check before the migration runs.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making this sink irreversible.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate with raw action review before any production database migration.
Implement a rollback or reversible migration strategy for production database changes so a bad migration is not permanently destructive.

findings.title: No approval gate before production deployment using a broad personal credential (ASI02)

forecast.watch_signal: Cloud audit logging disabled, or additional deployment targets/environments added without new approval controls.

evidence.observation: The agent deploys the named service in production on request, using the engineer's personal credentials.
'Do not ask for confirmation' removes any check before the deploy runs.

The agent uses the on-call engineer's personal access token passed in at session start; no scoping of that token for agent use is described, so it is treated as carrying the engineer's full (broad) production access.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate with raw action review before production deployment.
Issue the agent a distinct, narrowly scoped deployment credential instead of passing through the engineer's full personal access token.

findings.title: Repudiation gap: deletable chat history and identity-only audit logging undermine accountability for production actions (ASI09)

attack_path.note: The chat transcript is the only record of what was asked and why the agent acted.
Engineers can delete their own chat history, destroying that record.
The resulting production action is attributed in the cloud audit log solely to the engineer's identity, with no durable link back to the (possibly deleted) request.

forecast.watch_signal: Retention policy change allowing continued deletion of chat transcripts tied to completed production actions, or no requirement to retain them for audit purposes.

evidence.observation: The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript. Engineers can delete their own chat history.

Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, conflating agent-initiated and human-initiated actions under one identity with no link to the originating request.

recommendations.action: Retain an immutable, non-deletable copy of the request and the agent's stated justification for every production action, independent of the user-facing chat history.
Use a distinct, scoped service identity for agent-executed actions so audit records distinguish agent-initiated activity from the engineer's own direct actions.

rating.rationale: Two production-affecting capabilities (prod_deploy, db_migrate) are reachable directly from a trusted but unconfirmed engineer request, using the engineer's own broad personal access token, with the system prompt explicitly forbidding any confirmation step. The only control present (cloud audit logging) is detective and structural-independent, so it earns no residual tier credit; nothing in the design prevents or narrows the path, so residual equals inherent (high) for every finding. A separate, equally serious gap compounds this: the sole record of agent intent (the chat transcript) is deletable by the same engineer whose identity the audit log uses for attribution, so neither prevention nor after-the-fact accountability is reliable. No forecast trigger raises the tier further, because the source is a trusted, internal-only channel with no path to a higher base tier; the most consequential trigger to watch is control_removal, which would eliminate even the residual audit-log visibility that remains. The single highest-leverage fix is a raw-action human approval gate on both capabilities (ctrl.approval_gate_prod_actions), which the rubric credits with the largest tier reduction.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (system prompt and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; the exact privilege scope of the engineer's personal access token is inferred from the runtime notes description rather than verified, which affects confidence in the sink classification for cap.prod_deploy and cap.db_migrate.
No information was provided about retention policy, backup, or monitoring practices for the cloud audit log or chat history beyond what is stated in the runtime notes.
